body.text:
Done — all of `ASK_TOOLS.md` §8 is built, tested, and verified live.

## The acceptance test passes

```bash
git for-ai ask "tell me what changed in the last commit"
```

It called `commit_diff`, read the real patch, and answered by name: `architecture/ASK_TOOLS.md` (new, +160 lines) and `architecture/ROADMAP.md` (+8), "no implementation code changed in this commit." Footer:

```
Consulted:
  git show HEAD
Confidence: high (read directly from the repository, not from similarity alone)
```

Ref byte-identity checked around a second live run — `git for-each-ref` unchanged, so the non-minting guarantee survives the tool loop.

## What landed

- **Core** ([synthesis.ts](packages/core/src/query/synthesis.ts)) — `SynthesisTool`, the agentic loop, `tool-iteration-cap` skip reason, `toolCalls` provenance on `SynthesisResult`, usage summed across round trips. Assistant turns are echoed back verbatim (thinking blocks included), all `tool_result` blocks go back in one user message, a throwing tool returns `is_error` and is recorded.
- **§6** — `renderSource` now renders the ledger entry's `scope`. That was the actual root cause: the per-file "what changed" list was retrieved and then dropped.
- **CLI** ([askTools.ts](packages/cli/src/commands/askTools.ts)) — `commit_diff`, `show_change`, `log_intent`, `blame_why`, each wrapping the identical pure function its command wraps, output capped at 20k chars with an explicit truncation notice. Wired into `ask`, `/api/ask`, and inherited by `mcp`.
- **Surfaces** — CLI gets a `Consulted:` block; `/api/ask` gets `synthesis.consulted`; the review panel renders "Also checked: the changes in ce23522" (product language, no tool names).
- **Tests** — 688 passing, 4 skipped, 0 failing (up from ~570). The whole loop is driven through `fetchImpl`; the toolbox is tested against real fixture repos.
- **Docs** — ARCHITECTURE §11.5 (new), CLI_REFERENCE ask section, REVIEW_UI amendment, ROADMAP marked shipped, ASK_TOOLS status header.

## Your two flagged questions

**Model → `claude-sonnet-5`**, as you asked. One consequence I handled rather than assumed: Sonnet 5 runs adaptive thinking when `thinking` is omitted, and `max_tokens` caps thinking *plus* response text — so the per-request cap went 1024 → 4096. I deliberately send no `thinking` or `output_config` field: either would 400 on some models and turn `GIT_FOR_AI_SYNTHESIS_MODEL` into a footgun.

**Iteration cap — I made the call rather than blocking:** the *outcome* is visible, the *number* is not. Hitting it renders "the answer was still reading the repository when it hit the read limit" plus the ranked sources and the reads it did manage; `--json`/MCP carry `skippedReason` and full `toolCalls`. The count is our plumbing (rule 10); the incomplete answer is the user's problem. Say the word if you'd rather see "6 reads" on screen.

## Two things worth your attention

- **Cost per answer is now multi-request** — a tool-using answer is 2+ calls at Sonnet rates ($3/$15 per MTok, $2/$10 intro through 2026-08-31) versus Haiku's $1/$5 single call. Roughly 6–10× on tool-using questions. Worth watching before deciding it's the permanent default.
- **Sonnet writes long.** The live answer was ~20 lines despite the system prompt asking for "a few sentences." I left the prompt alone rather than retuning it behind your back — it's on the ROADMAP as a follow-up.

I haven't committed anything. Want me to?

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
ask stops refusing and goes and looks: it can read the repo itself

The live failure: "tell me what changed in the last commit" got an honest refusal,
because the only thing the model ever saw for HEAD was its eleven-word summary line.
Nothing in the index is keyed by commit, so no retrieval tuning could have fixed it.
Per ASK_TOOLS.md (and the owner's rejection of a pre-classify-and-stuff-context fix),
synthesis is now an agentic loop over the tool's own features.

Retrieval still runs first and still supplies numbered, citable sources — that part
works and is what makes answers verifiable. On top of it the model may call
commit_diff, show_change, log_intent or blame_why, each wrapping the IDENTICAL pure
function its CLI command wraps, so degradation messages and the non-minting read
guarantee are inherited rather than re-implemented. Core owns the interface and the
loop; the CLI injects the implementations (hard rule 6).

Acceptance test passes live against this repo: the question above now calls
commit_diff, reads the real patch, and names architecture/ASK_TOOLS.md and
architecture/ROADMAP.md with their line counts. Refs stay byte-identical across a
live run — ask is still a read.

Also in: ASK_TOOLS.md §6, rendering a ledger entry's `scope` (the per-file record of
WHAT changed, previously retrieved and then dropped on the floor); a `Consulted:`
block in the CLI, `synthesis.consulted` on /api/ask, and an "Also checked: …" line
in the review panel — an answer grounded in a live read is more verifiable than one
grounded in an embedding hit, so that gets surfaced, not hidden.

Judgment calls:

- Default model claude-haiku-4-5 -> claude-sonnet-5 (owner decision). The task
  changed under the model: no longer summarize-retrieved-text but decide-which-read-
  answers-this, and a wrong tool choice costs a round trip AND the answer. Knock-on:
  that model runs adaptive thinking when `thinking` is omitted and max_tokens covers
  thinking plus response text, so the per-request cap went 1024 -> 4096. The request
  body deliberately carries no thinking/output_config field — either would 400 on
  some models and break the GIT_FOR_AI_SYNTHESIS_MODEL escape hatch. Thinking blocks
  are echoed back verbatim in the loop, as that model requires.
- The iteration cap (6) is visible as an OUTCOME, never as a number: hitting it
  renders "still reading the repository when it hit the read limit" plus the ranked
  sources and the reads it managed. skippedReason "tool-iteration-cap" and full
  toolCalls go to --json/MCP. Rule 10 — the count is our plumbing.
- The caller's already-loaded embedder is threaded into blame_why, so a nested read
  never loads a second embedding model in a process that already has one (RAM rule).
- Tool output is capped at 20k chars with an explicit truncation notice; a throwing
  tool is reported to the model AND recorded as a failed read, never swallowed.

688 tests pass (4 skipped), up from ~570. The whole loop is driven through the
fetchImpl seam — the one sanctioned mock — and the toolbox is tested against real
fixture repos. Docs updated: ARCHITECTURE §11.5 (new), CLI_REFERENCE, REVIEW_UI,
ROADMAP marked shipped, ASK_TOOLS status header.

Built by the orchestrating session directly; no subagents.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
